topic: Extremal letter frequencies for one forbidden binary word: lengths one to three and reducible families
title: Boundary corrections and a length-three extension of Bóna–Maga–Richey's extremal-frequency analysis

creators.name: Zhang, Wenlin
creators.affiliation: National University of Singapore; ChronoAI Pte Ltd, Singapore

abstract: For Bóna, Maga and Richey's extremal-frequency question (arXiv:2606.06655v2, revised September 9, 2026, Section 5.3, p. 19), we extend the classical frequency calculations of Lekkerkerker (1951), Chang (1986) and Kovačević (2018/2019) to classify the maximizers at lengths one, two and three by exact counting and generating functions. They are 0, 00, and the pair 100,001, respectively: the first two lengths contradict the unrestricted proposal, whereas length three agrees with it. We prove the authors' reducible-word frequency identity with its necessary boundary restriction, obtain all four complementary families, and show that their candidate frequencies decrease strictly to 1/2. The comparison with all competitors at lengths at least four is separate.
summary: The maximizing forbidden words at lengths one, two and three are 0, 00, and 001 or 100. Classical run-frequency formulas give the three reducible families and their complements; their candidate values decrease strictly to 1/2. Written proofs give these comparisons, the exceptional length-two reduction and the singleton extension to any finite alphabet. The all-competitor comparison at lengths at least four is not established by these arguments.
